whyChoose.title: What Temple City Families Should Know

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible under narrower circumstances. An independent attorney can help sort out who in your family qualifies.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity, like a city road authority, is involved. Waiting to get guidance can cost a family its right to recover.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral costs and lost financial support, but also compensation for the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. A civil wrongful death case is separate from any criminal charges filed against a driver.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing depending on the specific family situation. An independent attorney can look at your circumstances and explain where your family stands.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Temple City?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. That deadline is much shorter, often just months, if the crash involved a government entity such as a city-maintained road. Because Temple City's crash counts show clustering near corridors like Lower Azusa Road and Temple City Boulevard, it's worth having an attorney check quickly whether a public entity may be involved.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they're entirely separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action a family pursues to recover financial losses and other damages. One can proceed regardless of the outcome of the other.
